_partNote: Six tiles of ordinary laboratory hardware, each a static object that sits still on a bench, chosen so no two share an outline: a scalloped row of small cones (PCR strip), a flat dot-grid slab (microplate), four long parallel bars (quadrupole), a rectangle with a canted neck (culture flask), a tall capped cylinder (blood tube), and a low round puck (wearable sensor). The microplate and the flask are the pair to watch, so the flask's angled neck is called out explicitly and the plate is kept strictly flat.

partPrompts.1: A strip of eight PCR tubes lying horizontally, seen three-quarter: eight identical small tubes molded together in a straight row, each tapering to a rounded point at the bottom so the lower outline is a run of even scallops, joined along the top by a continuous flat rib, and capped by a matching strip of eight domed lids sitting closed on top. Small, low and clearly a repeating row of eight. One strip only; not a rack, no instrument, no single tube on its own, no vessel and no equipment.
partPrompts.2: A microplate lying flat, seen three-quarter: a shallow rectangular tray with a plain flat skirt around its base and a low flat rim, its top face filled edge to edge with a regular grid of identical small round wells in straight rows and columns, one corner well drawn slightly clipped to mark the orientation. Strictly flat and low, wider than it is deep. One object only, lying on a plain surface; no lid, no neck, no spout, no opening on any side, nothing rising above the rim, no vessel and no equipment.
partPrompts.3: A spectrophotometer cuvette standing upright and open at the top, seen three-quarter: a small cell with a strictly square cross-section and four flat vertical walls meeting at four sharp vertical corners, roughly twice as tall as it is wide, with a plain flat square rim around its open mouth, a flat square base, and liquid filling the lower two-thirds to a flat level line. Boxy and straight-sided, drawn large and centered. One cuvette only; nothing round or cylindrical anywhere, no cap, no stopper, no lid, no neck, no coil, no spiral, no helix, no strand, no tube, no rods, no cage, no vessel and no equipment.
partPrompts.4: A cell culture flask lying flat, seen three-quarter: a shallow rectangular body with a flat bottom and flat top and softly rounded corners, and a short plain neck rising at a clear diagonal from one corner of the top face, angled away from the body and closed with a ribbed round cap. A shallow pool of liquid lies in the bottom of the body. The canted neck at the corner is what identifies it and must be clearly visible against the sky. One object only; no wells, no grid of holes, no dots on the top face, no dish, no other vessel.
partPrompts.5: A blood collection tube standing upright, seen three-quarter: a plain smooth straight-sided cylinder about five times taller than it is wide, closed at the bottom by a smooth round hemisphere and at the top by a thick raised stopper that is slightly wider than the tube and clearly proud of the rim, filled about two-thirds with liquid showing a flat level line. Tall, narrow and capped. One tube only; not a rack, no other tubes, no label, no needle, no holder, no cone, no taper, no vessel and no equipment.
partPrompts.6: A round wearable sensor patch, seen three-quarter from slightly above: a low circular puck much wider than it is tall, with a softly beveled top face, a thin flat adhesive rim extending a short way beyond the body all the way around, and one very fine straight filament projecting a short distance down from the center of its underside. Low, round and flat, like a button lying on a surface. One object only; no arm, no skin, no phone, no screen, no display, no text, no vessel and no equipment.
